raw_response:
I will still do mostly what I did in recent years, because at my age I do not like turning the whole place upside down. On 9 mu, I have to count every bag of fertilizer and every irrigation, but I also cannot risk cutting fertilizer too hard. If wheat is weak, the whole year is affected. If maize misses fertilizer at jointing, yield falls fast. Cotton takes more watching and more pesticide, so I will not put too much land into it. Around here, if neighbors use a better wheat seed or maize hybrid and I see it stands well and yields well, I will follow that. I have well irrigation, so I will use that advantage and not let the crop wait for rain too long. My way is simple: wheat gets enough base fertilizer and two waters, maize gets enough nitrogen after wheat and one or two waters, and cotton gets a bit more potassium and more spraying because insects can ruin it. This year I will keep 6 mu in wheat-maize rotation and 3 mu in cotton, so labor and spending stay within what my family can handle.
